scope: Stable opt-in XCTest presentation and bounded native tool-planner evidence experiments
sourceBinding: Final source hashes bind ui-test-policy-green-01 and default-test-policy-01. The three diagnostic stages added progressively more failure metadata and were not individually source-hashed. Exact commands, result bundles, identifiers, failure evidence and output hashes are retained.
policy: macOS MCP/native tools first; planning/context/answer errors are not demonstrated MCP incapability.
One build/test/inference at a time; Xcode jobs 1; no source edits during builds/tests.
12 GB whole-Mac target; one model worker, 2 threads, 4 GiB sampled stop, 8K context, 1024 output tokens, six proposals.
No production model-selection change, installation, purchases, messages, account login, pushes or release.

testHostPresentation.tested: Three failing combined batches localize windowNotActive; final combined 20 methods and default 3 methods pass, zero skips.
testHostPresentation.accepted: Scoped opt-in test-process policy and continued suppression of host services/chrome only.

controlledMCPBrowser.tested: 10.833716 seconds, correct departure/platform, one visit per page, actual MCP link verification, zero CU calls.

alternativeNativeToolPlanner.compiled: Python checks and actual b9992 load
alternativeNativeToolPlanner.tested: See model attempts; no production adapter

generalComputerUse.tested: Normal HostSession, varied public/native tasks, provider login/phone and whole-Mac resources remain open.

findings: The previous opaque InvalidTransition is now identified as ComputerUseBrowserError.windowNotActive during initial execution before any model call.

Third red run starts with accessory policy; setActivationPolicy(accessory) returns false and leaves accessory immediately, but failure later observes prohibited, no key window and Codex frontmost. The AI Browser exists and is visible. This supports delayed test-host activation-policy transitions as the cause of this combined-run failure.

RUN_COMPUTER_USE_UI_TESTS=1 applies only in XCTest. It establishes accessory policy before explicit native UI methods; default test mode remains prohibited. Neither mode starts production host services, chrome or automatic test windows.
Production browser focus/ownership checks, activation timing and window reuse are unchanged. This checkpoint does not claim the user-visible production flicker is fully qualified.
The final combined bundle retains a main-thread responsiveness warning; default three-method mode has no recorded runtime warnings.
Granite read the correct native date but generated a different one. Valid tool calls and a correct URL do not establish whole-goal correctness.
